Dialogue p41.text: Hoy en día, la gente ve nieblas no porque hay nieblas, sino porque los poetas y los pintores les han enseñado la misteriosa belleza de tales efectos.
Dialogue p41.alignment: The complete sentence corresponds to the original printed p. 41: people perceive fogs because poets and painters taught them the mysterious beauty of such effects, not because fogs exist. The article cites Langre 2002 pp. 111–113 as a range; this sentence’s exact book page and its typography have not been inspected. Italics in the article mark the longer quotation.

Personally read source-bound second PDF page 8, Logos printed p. 159, and the original 1905 printed p. 41: the complete Spanish sentence, accents and punctuation match the page, and preserve the contrast between the existence of fogs and perception taught by poets and painters. The article quotes a longer passage in italics and cites Langre 2002 pp. 111–113; the precise book page and original typography have not been inspected. Translator Luis Martínez Victorio is identified by the publisher and the Library of Congress authority for this edition.

mexico_quotation.assessment: Independent review: the exact 27-word sentence is a significant proposition, but its complete causal contrast is needed for the stated comparison with the English original. In the identified research display this isolated excerpt is proportionate to the longer translated essay and does not substitute for its normal exploitation; aggregation or changed commercial context requires a fresh assessment. The words and punctuation match the published secondary quotation, with whitespace normalized; cite Wilde, translator Luis Martínez Victorio, Langre 2002 and Logos 2025 p. 159. The original book, its exact page within pp. 111–113 and its typography were not inspected; article-wide quotation italics are not asserted to be the book typography. This assessment applies to Mexico LFDA 148(I) only and assumes the actual display retains those conditions.
